annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (UK Government)
key_provisions_or_claims: Five non-statutory cross-sectoral principles: safety/security/robustness, transparency/explainability, fairness, accountability/governance, contestability/redress.
Existing regulators apply the principles in context; no new AI regulator is created.
AI defined by adaptivity and autonomy rather than rigid legal definitions.
Anticipated statutory duty on regulators to have due regard to principles, if monitoring shows it is needed.
Central functions: monitoring and evaluation, risk assessment, horizon scanning, sandboxes, education, international interoperability.
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: UK Government white paper setting a pro-innovation, context-based AI regulatory framework. Five non-statutory cross-sectoral principles are applied by existing regulators, supported by central functions for monitoring, risk assessment, sandboxes and international interoperability, with no new AI regulator and no initial legislation. Robotics appears only in passing examples.
annotation.title_clean: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
annotation.title_en: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
